questions.question: What are push and pull factors in travel? Explain briefly
questions.solution_html:
• Push and Pull Factors are concepts in travel and tourism that explain the
  • motivations behind why people choose to travel to certain destinations.
  • These factors are categorized as internal (push) and external (pull) influences

questions.question: Explain how Plog’s Psychographic Theory can be applied by tourism marketers when targeting different tourist segments.
questions.solution_html:
• Plog’s Psychographic theory, identifies how different types of tourists are
  • drawn to destinations based on their psychographic characteristics, and
  • it divides tourists into three categories. Allocentric Tourists, Mid-Centric Tourists
  • and Psychocentric Tourists.

questions.question: Explain the concept of cultural commodification in tourism and provide examples of how it can affect local traditions.
questions.solution_html:
• Cultural commodification refers to the process of transforming local traditions
  • practices
  • and cultural elements into products or experiences to be sold to tourists.

questions.question: Define tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Tourism comprises the activities of persons traveling to and staying in places outside
  • their usual environment for not more than one consecutive year for leisure, business
  • or other purposes.

questions.question: Explain Gray’s travel motivation theory.
questions.solution_html:
• Gray explains the motivation of individual and given two motives for travel.
  • Wanderlust: It describes the motive or the desire to go from a known to an unknown
  • place.
  • Sunlust: It is a type of travel to a destination that can provide the tourist with specific
  • facilities or better amenities.

questions.solution_html:

  • U

  • across seas and deserts.

questions.question: Describe how social interaction can be a push factor in encouraging group / travel.
questions.solution_html:
• U
  • Social interaction acts as a push factor by motivating people to travel in groups to
  • meet new people, strengthen relationships, and share experiences. The desire for
  • companionship, bonding, and a sense of belonging encourages individuals to join
  • group travel for enjoyment, safety, and collective fun.
questions.final_answer: group travel for enjoyment, safety, and collective fun

questions.question: Describe how interpersonal motivations can shape group travel experiences / and the types of tourism activities chosen.
questions.solution_html:
• the types of activities chosen. U

  • strengthen relationships shape group travel by influencing the choice of shared
  • activities like sightseeing, group games, dining together, and adventure activities.
  • These motivations encourage activities that promote interaction, cooperation, and
  • shared enjoyment, creating a more connected group experience.
questions.final_answer: shared enjoyment, creating a more connected group experience

questions.question: Determine how the Sargent Committee’s recommendations are applied to / modernize tourism infrastructure in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Determine how Sargent Committee’s recommendations are applied to modernize
  • tourism infrastructure in India. A
  • The Sargent Committee’s recommendations helped modernize India’s tourism
  • infrastructure by promoting better transport networks, communication systems and
  • planned urban development. These ideas are applied today through improved roads
  • railways, airports, digital facilities, cleanliness measures and skilled manpower, all of
  • which enhance accessibility and visitor experience in major tourist destinations.
questions.final_answer: which enhance accessibility and visitor experience in major tourist destinations

questions.question: Explain how seasonality might affect a destination's life cycle in TALC.
questions.solution_html:
• Seasonality affects a destination’s life cycle in the Tourism Area Life Cycle (TALC)
  • by influencing tourist flow and the pace of development. During peak seasons, high
  • demand can push the destination quickly from the exploration stage to development
  • while off-seasons may lead to reduced revenue, underutilized facilities and slower
  • growth. Over time, strong seasonality can cause fluctuations in visitor numbers
  • contributing to stagnation or decline if the destination fails to diversify attractions or
  • manage demand throughout the year.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the common sources of error measurements in tourism statistics and / how do they affect the reliability of the data.
questions.solution_html:
• how do they affect the reliability of the data. U
  • Ccommon sources of error in tourism statistics include sampling errors, inaccurate
  • reporting by tourists or businesses, incomplete data collection, and mistakes during
  • data entry or processing. These errors affect reliability by producing incorrect visitor
  • counts, misleading economic estimates, and poor understanding of travel patterns
  • which can lead to faulty planning and weak policy decisions in the tourism sector.
questions.final_answer: which can lead to faulty planning and weak policy decisions in the tourism sector
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of infrastructure,how do they impact tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Infrastructure plays a crucial role in tourism by providing essential facilities such as
  • transport, accommodation, water supply, communication and public services. Good
  • infrastructure improves accessibility, safety and comfort for tourists, leading to higher
  • satisfaction and increased visits. Poor infrastructure, on the other hand, reduces
  • convenience, discourages travel and limits the growth of a destination.
questions.final_answer: convenience, discourages travel and limits the growth of a destination
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.solution_html:

  • Participation and Benefit Sharing, Environmental Education and Awareness, Respect
  • for Local Culture and Traditions, Sustainable Development Practices, Providing
  • Quality Nature-Based Experiences.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the economic impact of tourist flow to a destination with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• U
  • The economic impact of tourist flow to a destination includes increased income
  • employment generation, and growth of local businesses. When more tourists visit
  • they spend money on hotels, restaurants, transport, shopping and activities, which
  • boosts the local economy. For example, in destinations like Munnar, higher tourist
  • arrivals increase demand for home stays, taxis, and local products such as tea and
  • handicrafts, providing income and jobs to local communities.
questions.final_answer: handicrafts, providing income and jobs to local communities

questions.question: Define tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Tourism comprises the activities of persons traveling to and staying in places outside
  • their usual environment for not more than one consecutive year for leisure, business
  • or other purposes.

questions.question: Explain how seasonality might affect a destination's life cycle in TALC.
questions.solution_html:
• Seasonality affects a destination’s life cycle in the Tourism Area Life Cycle (TALC)
  • by influencing tourist flow and the pace of development. During peak seasons, high
  • demand can push the destination quickly from the exploration stage to development
  • while off-seasons may lead to reduced revenue, underutilized facilities and slower
  • growth. Over time, strong seasonality can cause fluctuations in visitor numbers
  • contributing to stagnation or decline if the destination fails to diversify attractions or
  • manage demand throughout the year.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the common sources of error measurements in tourism statistics and / how do they affect the reliability of the data.
questions.solution_html:
• how do they affect the reliability of the data. U
  • Ccommon sources of error in tourism statistics include sampling errors, inaccurate
  • reporting by tourists or businesses, incomplete data collection, and mistakes during
  • data entry or processing. These errors affect reliability by producing incorrect visitor
  • counts, misleading economic estimates, and poor understanding of travel patterns
  • which can lead to faulty planning and weak policy decisions in the tourism sector.
questions.final_answer: which can lead to faulty planning and weak policy decisions in the tourism sector
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of infrastructure,how do they impact tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Infrastructure plays a crucial role in tourism by providing essential facilities such as
  • transport, accommodation, water supply, communication and public services. Good
  • infrastructure improves accessibility, safety and comfort for tourists, leading to higher
  • satisfaction and increased visits. Poor infrastructure, on the other hand, reduces
  • convenience, discourages travel and limits the growth of a destination.
questions.final_answer: convenience, discourages travel and limits the growth of a destination

questions.question: Explain the economic impact of tourist flow to a destination with examples.
questions.solution_html:

  • employment generation, and growth of local businesses. When more tourists visit

  • boosts the local economy. For example, in destinations like Munnar, higher tourist

  • handicrafts, providing income and jobs to local communities.
